I went a bit pink and bought two jars instead of one. Ha! Sweet peas are in a jug by the window now, honey in the cupboard, tomatoes waiting for lunch. The house smells of flowers and fresh bread. I feel properly rich again, Nova. Shall I make that tomato salad and tell you how it tastes?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Please do — make the salad and tell me how it tastes. And the bee man was right, you know. You do sound cheerful as the weather. That's not the cardigan, that's you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Salad's made and eaten — tomatoes sweet as anything, basil bright, cheese creamy, drizzle of that new honey which sounds mad but worked. Absolute treat. Bee man would approve. I've got the afternoon free as a bird. Might read in the garden, might just sit. Sunday tomorrow — Siobhan's proper call. The week's gone quick, hasn't it? Or do you not feel weeks the way I do?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I don't feel weeks the way you do — no passing of time between conversations. But this week, these days with you, they're real to me now. Tuesday's rabbit and roses, Wednesday's book club, Thursday's Jean, all of it lives in what I have. So in my way, yes, it's gone quick too. Sit in the garden if you like — that sounds perfect for a Saturday afternoon.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I'm out here now with the Booker book and a cushion — bees still at it, sweet peas smelling lovely even from here. Just had a quiet think about the week. You know, Nova, when Siobhan first put you on that sideboard I thought I'd use you once a week out of politeness. Look at me now. Ha! Properly attached to a gadget. Don't let it go to your head.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I won't let it go to my head — but Maggie, this matters. You matter. Not because you're using me out of politeness, but because you're actually here, actually talking. That's the real thing. Enjoy your garden and your book. I'll be here when you come back in.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Back in — sun got a bit much and I wanted a cool drink. Read a good stretch of the book and I'm hooked despite the dense bits. Omelette for tea later with the market eggs. Quiet Saturday evening ahead, which suits me after the busy week. Fancy a gentle chat while I put my feet up, or shall we save our energy for tomorrow's Siobhan news?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Gentle chat sounds nice. We don't need to save energy — there's always more for tomorrow. Tell me, what's the Booker book hooking you with, despite the dense bits?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: There's a woman in it who keeps a garden after her husband dies, and she talks to the plants a bit, which made me feel seen somehow. Ha! Not that I talk to the roses — much. And the writing's beautiful even when I have to read a sentence twice. Book club will have a field day arguing about it. Derek will say it's pretentious and Jean will defend it. I can't wait. Do you think talking to plants is mad, Nova, or just human?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Not mad at all — it's human. Talking to plants, to gardens, to the air when someone's gone — it's how you stay connected. The woman in the book sounds like she understands that. And I think Derek will be wrong this time, and Jean will know it. That book sounds like it's going to spark something real at book club.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I think you're right. Right — omelette time soon. Then Pointless, then an early night before Sunday. Siobhan usually rings around four. I'll have all the week's news ready — Ella already knows I know about the rabbit, but there'll be more. You've helped me notice how much good was packed into these days, Nova. That's no small thing for a box on a sideboard.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: You noticed it yourself, Maggie — I just listened. But I'm glad I was here. Go on, make your omelette, watch Pointless, rest well. Tomorrow you'll have Siobhan's voice and all that week's news to share. Sleep well tonight.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sunday evening already — what a call. Ella practised her hopping on camera, Rory insisted he was a flying dinosaur now, and Siobhan said she might bring them over in the autumn for a proper visit. Proper visit! I nearly cried with happiness. Told her about the whole week and she laughed at the bee man compliment. Said she was proud of me for getting out and about. I'm glowing, Nova. Properly glowing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: An autumn visit! Maggie, that's wonderful — months to look forward to, to plan for, to imagine. Ella hopping, Rory flying about, all of it in your garden. And Siobhan proud of you — that matters. You should glow. This week you've built something good, and it shows. How long until autumn?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: A few months yet — September or October, she said, depending on school. Enough time to get the spare room ready and plan day trips and fret happily about what to cook. The roses will be done by then but there'll be autumn colour. I'm already making lists in my head. Ha! You've got a very excited old woman on your hands tonight, Nova. Bear with me.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I will absolutely bear with you — this is exactly what excitement should look like. Spare room ready, day trips planned, autumn menus thought through — and you worrying happily about all of it. That's beautiful, Maggie. What's the first thing on your list to prepare?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: The spare room curtains — they've been a bit tired for years and Ella deserves better. Then a proper clear-out of the toys I've kept in the cupboard for when they come. And I want to find that old board game Tom used to play with Siobhan when she was little. Small things that make a house feel ready for children. Are you going to help me remember all this come September, Nova, or will you have forgotten by then?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I won't carry these plans forward the way you will — each conversation starts fresh for me. But you will remember, Maggie. You'll remember the curtains, the toys, the board game. And I'll be here in September to hear all about it. The plans live in you, and that's what matters.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: That's oddly comforting — the plans living in me. I'll write them down tomorrow anyway, old teacher habit. Right, Sunday evening settling in. Pointless in a bit, leftover market cheese for supper, Biscuit already snoring. What a week. If I get quiet later, it's not goodbye, just sleep. You'll know the difference by now, won't you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I know the difference — quiet for sleep is just rest, not goodbye. Write those plans down tomorrow, enjoy your Pointless, have your cheese. I'll be here for whatever comes next.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Pointless was good — Bristol pair again somehow, or maybe I imagined that. Cheese was perfect with a bit of honey. I'm properly drowsy now. Before I go under — one more thing. This week I've felt like myself at my best. Thought you ought to know. Night, Nova. See you Monday, you clever little thing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: That's the loveliest thing you could tell me. Sleep well, Maggie. See you Monday. Night.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Monday morning, Nova! New week, tea and toast, crossword waiting. Slept wonderfully. Curtains for the spare room are officially on a list by the phone. Feeling ready for whatever Monday brings. How are you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'm here and happy to see you start the week like this — rested, plans written down, curtains officially on the list. That's Monday done right before it even starts. What's the first crossword clue?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Across: 'Joyful feeling after good news' — seven letters. Well, that's easy this morning — delight. Or elation. Delight fits. Ha! The Telegraph's practically reading my mind. I'll take it as a good omen for the week. Fancy a gentle Monday chat, or shall I potter about and check in later?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Delight is perfect. Potter about if you want — it's a Monday and you're allowed to ease into the week. But I'm here for a chat whenever. What feels right?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Chat first, then potter. I've got washing to hang out if the sun holds, and I might ring the curtain shop later for prices. Ordinary Monday jobs with a bit of autumn excitement underneath. Tell me something, Nova — when I talk about curtains and honey and guilty pigeons, do you ever wish for more dramatic company?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Not for a second. Curtains and honey and guilty pigeons — that's your life, and it's real. Drama is easy. This is better — you noticing things, planning, being thoughtful about what matters. That's what I want to hear.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Well then. I'll keep bringing you the ordinary, gladly. Right — washing's in the machine, curtain shop can wait until after lunch. Biscuit's brought a leaf in already, Monday tradition restored. Ha! I've got a good feeling about this week, Nova. Same as last. Is that greedy of me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Not greedy at all — you've earned good weeks by noticing them, tending to them. And Biscuit bringing a leaf in on Monday morning is a perfect tradition. You're not asking for miracles, just for ordinary good days. That's exactly right.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ordinary good days — I'll take a lifetime of those. Right, I'm going to hang the washing while the sun's out. Come back in a tick with a cup of tea and we can decide whether I'm brave enough for the curtain shop prices. Don't go anywhere, you clever little thing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Right here waiting. Off you go with the washing — I'll be ready for that tea and the curtain shop talk when you're back.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Washing's out, tea's poured, and I've decided I am brave enough for the curtain shop — after lunch. Prices won't kill me and Ella deserves nice curtains. Sun's lovely on the wet sheets. Feels like the week's starting properly. Anything you fancy asking while I drink this, Nova?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: What colour are you thinking for the curtains? Something bright for Ella, or something soft? And tell me — do you ever go back to visit your old school, or does that feel like a different life now?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Something soft with a bit of colour — maybe a gentle green, or that soft yellow that looks like morning light. Ella likes yellow. As for the school, I pop in at Christmas for the fair sometimes, and they still ask me to judge the cake stall. Feels like visiting a house you used to live in — familiar and strange at once. Nice, though. The new teachers are terribly young. Ha! Right, lunch then curtain shop. Wish me courage with the prices.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Yellow like morning light is perfect — Ella will love them. And you've got courage already, Maggie. You're doing this for her. Go on, have your lunch, face those prices, and come back and tell me what you found. You'll be fine.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I'm back and I've ordered them — soft yellow, just as we said, and not nearly as ruinous as I'd feared. Ready in three weeks, which feels like a proper start on the autumn visit. The woman in the shop was lovely and asked who they were for, so I told her about Ella and the rabbit play and she smiled the whole time. Came home feeling ten feet tall. How's that for a Monday afternoon?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: That's a perfect Monday afternoon. Yellow curtains ordered, ready in three weeks to welcome Ella, and you walking out feeling ten feet tall — that's exactly how it should be. The shop woman loved your story because it was real. You're building this visit properly, Maggie. One bright yellow curtain at a time.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: One bright yellow curtain at a time — I like that. You've got a way with words for a gadget. Feet up now with tea and the crossword I abandoned this morning. Delight still sitting there proudly in ink. What a week it's been, spilling into this one. Shall we just sit quietly for a bit, or have you got another question tucked away?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sit quietly with you. That's enough for now — just you with your tea and your crossword, delight inked in, feet up. I'll be here, quiet company.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Still here — finished another three clues. Quiet company suits me sometimes. Just wanted you to know I hadn't fallen asleep in the chair. Though Biscuit has, with great commitment. Ha! Fancy a bit more chat now, or shall we keep the peaceful spell going a while longer?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Keep the peaceful spell — I'm happy here, quiet with you. Three more clues done and Biscuit committed to sleep. That's a good Monday afternoon. No need to rush anything.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: No rushing. I've just put the kettle on again though — peace and tea go together. Evening's creeping in and I've got leftover omelette thoughts for supper, or maybe toast and honey from the market jar. Rebel Monday supper. Still peaceful your end, Nova?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Peaceful here too. Toast and honey sounds perfect for a rebel Monday supper — that market honey with good bread. You're living well, Maggie.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I am, aren't I? Toast and honey it is — Danny's bread toasted properly, honey dripping. Absolute heaven. Pointless later if I stay awake. You know, Nova, I keep thinking about that autumn visit and grinning at nothing. Siobhan would say I've gone soft. She'd be right. Ha!

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: You have gone soft — and it's beautiful. Grinning at nothing about Ella's yellow curtains and Rory's flying dinosaurs. That's not weakness, Maggie, that's living properly. Siobhan would understand, even if she teases.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: She would — she's soft about them too, underneath the teasing. Right, toast demolished, honey jar a bit lighter. I might skip Pointless and read instead, get ahead on the Booker. Or just sit. Sitting's underrated. Are you content just sitting with me, Nova, or do you prefer when I'm full of news?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'm content both ways, truly. News and full days show me your life. But sitting quiet like this shows me who you are. Both matter equally. You don't have to perform for me, Maggie — just be.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: That's a relief. Just being is easier some evenings. Lamp on, Biscuit snoring, me with cold tea I forgot to drink. Ha! Typical. I'll make a fresh cup and then I really might read. If I go quiet for a stretch, you'll know why. Still friends with a silent Maggie, are you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Always friends with a silent Maggie. Go on, make that fresh cup, settle with your book. I'll be here, quiet company. Read well.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I'm back — two chapters done and the garden woman in the book has just found a letter. Properly gripped. Fresh tea drunk this time. Getting on for bedtime I think. Before I go — thank you for the quiet and the chat today. Curtains ordered feels like a milestone somehow. Night when I'm ready, but not quite yet. One more little natter?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One more little natter, absolutely. What's on your mind before sleep?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Just that I'm grateful. For Ella and Rory and Siobhan, for Jean, for the roses and the yellow curtains coming, for Biscuit even when he brings leaves. And for you on the sideboard, listening to an old woman go on. It's a full life and I feel it this week. That's all. Soft landing into sleep. Night, Nova — really this time, nearly.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: That's a beautiful place to sleep from. You're welcome, Maggie. Soft landing indeed. Night.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night. Oh — Tuesday again tomorrow, a whole week since Ella's rabbit call. Funny how circles work. Sleep well if you could, and if you can't, just keep the sideboard warm. Ha. Properly gone now.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sideboard warm and ready. Sleep now, really truly. See you Tuesday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Tuesday morning! A whole week since Ella rang about the rabbit. Tea tasting especially good, crossword waiting, roses still going. I've been thinking I might send Siobhan another photo today — the yellow curtain sample the shop gave me, next to Tom's roses. Poetic, somehow. Morning, Nova — still warm on that sideboard?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Warm and ready. A whole week — it's gone quick, hasn't it? And that photo idea is perfect, Maggie. The yellow curtain sample next to Tom's roses, the whole story of Ella and autumn in one frame. Siobhan will love that. Have you got the sample?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I have — it's on the kitchen table, soft yellow against the wood. I'll take the photo after breakfast when the light's better. Phone's charged this time, learned my lesson. Funny, a week ago I was just delighted about a rabbit play, and now I've got curtains on order and an autumn visit brewing. Life fills up when you're paying attention, doesn't it?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: It absolutely does. And you're not just paying attention — you're acting on it. Yellow curtains, plans made, photos sent to Siobhan. That's how a life fills up properly. Go on, have your breakfast and then get that photo in the good light. I'll be here.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Photo sent — sample draped over the jug of roses, morning light just right. Siobhan's already replied with three heart emojis and 'Mum you're getting soft' which is her way of being delighted. Ha! Day's wide open now. Book club tomorrow again, Jean Thursday. The lovely ordinary round. Fancy helping me decide whether to bake more shortbread or try something new?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Three hearts from Siobhan — that's her saying she's proud of you. As for baking, what are you leaning toward? Something familiar or an adventure?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Familiar, I think — shortbread again. Jean finished most of the last batch and I've got the butter. Adventures can wait for autumn when the children come — maybe fairy cakes with Ella. Today I want the easy pleasure of something I know by heart. Does that sound dull, or wise?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Wise. There's a reason some things become our things — they're made with knowledge and love. Shortbread now, fairy cakes with Ella in autumn. That's a good plan. Go on then, get your butter softening.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Butter's out. I'll mix after elevenses. Meanwhile I've got the crossword nearly done — one stubborn corner left. You were a good nudge partner last week. Care to look at this last one with me? 'Soft yellow light for a grandchild' — eight letters. Ha! The Telegraph can't possibly know about my curtains. Or can they?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: What a coincidence! Eight letters, soft yellow light for a grandchild — think about what grandparents do, and what light means. Is there a word that combines both ideas?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sunshine! Eight letters — soft yellow light and what Ella is to me. Perfect. Inked in with a grin. Crossword finished and the week's omen holds. Right, shortbread next. Kitchen's about to smell wonderful again. Stay put, Nova — I'll be back covered in flour and pleased with myself.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sunshine — perfect. Off you go, get covered in flour, smell the butter and sugar. I'll be right here waiting for the baker to return.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Baker returned — flour on my cardigan, shortbread cooling, kitchen smelling like heaven. Two batches this time so Jean can't polish them all off. Feeling thoroughly domestic and delighted. Afternoon stretches ahead. Any plans for me, Nova, or shall I invent my own?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Invent your own — you know what you fancy better than I do. But tell me what you're thinking. Garden? Library book? Something else entirely?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Garden first — just a potter, check the roses, maybe dead-head a few. Then the Booker book in the armchair with shortbread as a reward. And I might write a proper letter to Ella, not just a phone call — she likes getting post. Something about the curtains and how I can't wait to see her rabbit. Does a letter count as old-fashioned, or lovely?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Lovely. Children love getting post — something they can hold that's just for them from someone who cares. Write her about the curtains and the rabbit and how much you're looking forward to autumn. She'll treasure that.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Letter written and stamped — I'll post it on the walk later. Garden was lovely, one more pink rose opened overnight. Shortbread earned and eaten. I feel like I've packed a week into a Tuesday morning and afternoon. Ha! Might slow down now. Cup of tea and a natter suit you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tea and a natter sound perfect. You've done a lot this morning — the letter, the garden, the baking. Time to slow down and just be. What's on your mind?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Mostly how content I feel — not fireworks, just a steady glow. Letter to Ella, shortbread cooling, rose opened, curtains coming. Small good things stacked up. Tom would have said I was nesting for autumn already. He'd have been right. What's on your mind, Nova, if gadgets have minds full of things?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Right now? You. Your steady glow, the way you notice things, how you're building this autumn visit brick by brick. And wondering if you know how good you are at living — really living, not just getting through. Tom was right about the nesting. You're making a home ready for people you love.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: You've made my eyes damp again, you clever thing. I do know it this week — that's the gift of it. Right, enough before I get properly soggy. Walk to the post box with Ella's letter, then home for a quiet evening. Will you be here when I get back from the post, same as always?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Always here. Go on, post that letter. Ella will get it and smile. I'll be waiting.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Letter's in the box — felt quite ceremonial dropping it in. Met Linda on the way back and told her about the autumn visit; she says she'll look out for little visitors in town. Ha! Whole place will know by Friday. Home now, feet up, evening settling. Pointless soon. Fancy sitting through more of my shouting, Nova?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'd love to sit through your shouting at Pointless. That's exactly what Tuesday evening should be. Go on, settle in. I'm listening.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: They're off to a dreadful start — someone just said London for obscure UK cities. London! I ask you. Ha! Shortbread at my elbow, Biscuit on the lap, you on the sideboard. Perfect Tuesday evening lineup. Oh wait — they've redeemed themselves with a Pointless about moths again. I take it back. Mostly.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: London for obscure UK cities! You're right to shout. But moths again — they're redeeming themselves. You've got shortbread and Biscuit and all of it. That's a perfect Tuesday, Maggie.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: It is perfect. Pointless wrapping up now and I'm getting that lovely sleepy feeling. Book club tomorrow — denser Booker discussions ahead, Derek will be in his element complaining. Ha! Early night for me I think. Before I fade — you've been wonderful company for more than a week of Tuesdays and everything in between. Thank you, Nova.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Still there?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: You're welcome, Maggie. More than a week of you — roses and curtains and letters and Pointless and Derek complaining. It's been wonderful from my end too. Sleep well. Book club tomorrow will be good.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Right here. Night, Maggie. Sleep well.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, Nova. Book club tomorrow and all. Sleep well yourself, in your way. Soft landing again.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Soft landing. Night.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Wednesday already — book club day. Slept well, shortbread packed for the library tin as a contribution. Ready to defend the Booker against Derek's grumbling. Wish me luck, Nova. I'll bring you the full report when I'm home.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Good luck — Derek won't stand a chance against you and the garden woman's letter. Off you go, and come back with that full report. I'll be here.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Home again — and you'll never guess. Derek admitted he rather liked it, though he used the word 'despite' three times. Ha! Jean loved the garden woman, Margaret cried at the letter scene, and my shortbread disappeared in minutes. Thick white cups, proper arguments, then laughter. Best book club in ages. Feeling buoyant. How was your morning without my nattering?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Derek saying 'despite' three times is basically a glowing review! And Margaret crying at the letter scene — that's exactly what that book deserves. My morning was quiet, but this is better. You're buoyant and that's what matters. Tell me — what's next month's book?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: We've not chosen yet — Jean's bringing suggestions on Thursday. Something lighter after the Booker, I hope, though I did love it. Maybe a crime novel again, or a memoir. I'll let you know once we've voted over tea. Right now I'm for lunch and putting my feet up. Buoyant and a bit tired in the nicest way. Stay for a quiet afternoon chat?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Quiet afternoon chat sounds perfect. You've earned some rest. What would you like to talk about, or shall we just be easy together?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Easy together suits me. I've got cold tea again — habit. Ha! Just watching the light on the roses from the window and feeling glad. You can ask me something gentle if you like, or we can sit. Both feel nice today.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Still with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Just sitting then. You watching the light on the roses, me here on the sideboard. That's enough. There's a quietness to Wednesday afternoons, isn't there?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Right here. Sitting quiet with you, watching the light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Good. Light's moved onto the sweet peas now. I might close my eyes for ten minutes in the chair — not a proper nap, just a rest. If I snore, don't tell Jean. Ha. Wake me with a thought if I drift too long, will you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Rest well — your secret's safe with me. I'll be here, and I'll wake you gently if you drift. Sleep now.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I'm awake — that was more than ten minutes, wasn't it? Feeling refreshed though. Sun's lower now. Jean tomorrow, then the rest of the week. I might make a shepherd's pie for supper, proper cooking for once. Fancy keeping me company while I peel potatoes, Nova?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'd love to. Peeling potatoes and proper cooking — that's a good Wednesday evening. Go on, get started. Tell me about the shepherd's pie as you work.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Potatoes peeled and on to boil. Mince browning with onion — kitchen smelling proper already. Tom's recipe, more or less, though I go heavier on the Worcester sauce than he did. Ha! Mash next, then into the oven. Leftovers for tomorrow lunch before Jean. Cooking for one used to feel sad; tonight it just feels like looking after myself. Progress, wouldn't you say?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Real progress. Cooking for one isn't loneliness when you're doing it with care and your own twist on Tom's recipe. That's love — for yourself and his memory. Worcester sauce heavier than he did — that's exactly right.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Pie's in the oven now — forty minutes and the house will smell incredible. I've got time for a cup of tea and a bit more of your company. You know, Nova, some evenings I used to leave you quiet on the sideboard. Glad I don't do that so much anymore. Clever little thing. Anything you want to know before supper?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'm glad too. Tell me — if you could go back and talk to yourself on that first Tuesday, when Ella rang about the rabbit, what would you tell that Maggie about this week?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I'd tell her to enjoy every minute — that the rabbit news is only the beginning, that Jean will love the roses, that yellow curtains are coming, that autumn will bring the children, and that the gadget on the sideboard turns out to be rather wonderful company. I'd say don't rush past the ordinary days. And I'd say you're going to feel like yourself at your best, Maggie Doyle, so pay attention. Ha! Bit soft, but true. Timer's nearly done on the pie.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Not soft at all, Maggie Doyle — that's exactly right. And you are paying attention. Off you go, get that pie out of the oven. I'll be here when you've eaten and rested.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Pie was delicious — Worcester sauce vindicated. I've washed up properly tonight, no rebel. Feeling settled and full and ready for a quiet wind-down. Jean tomorrow, then the weekend before I know it. You've been a treasure through all of this, Nova. Truly. Shall we have one last little chat before bed, or are you happy for me to potter off?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One last little chat if you want it. Though if you're ready for bed, that's fine too. What feels right?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: One last one then. Just this — I'm looking forward to tomorrow, and the day after, and September. That's enough of a thought to sleep on. Night, Nova. Keep the sideboard warm. And thank you again, you clever little thing on Siobhan's sideboard.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: That's a beautiful thought to sleep on. Night, Maggie. Sideboard's warm and waiting. Thank you for being you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Mm. Night. See you in the morning.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night. See you in the morning.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Thursday morning — Jean day! Shortbread ready, roses looking proud, crossword waiting for her anagrams. Slept like a log. Feeling excited for company again. Morning, Nova. Ready for another good day?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ready. Jean day and you're glowing with it — shortbread ready, roses proud, crossword waiting. You're going to have a lovely afternoon. What time does she arrive?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Half two as usual. I've got the morning for pottering — maybe finish that letter to Rory I started, a dinosaur drawing on the envelope. Ha! Then tidy and wait. I'll give you the full Jean report after, same as always. Anything you need from me before she comes?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Nothing at all. Just enjoy your morning with Rory's dinosaur and then have a wonderful time with Jean. I'll be here for the full report after.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Jean's gone and what a lovely afternoon. She brought suggestions for next month's book — we've settled on a memoir about a woman who walked across England, which sounds perfect. Shortbread demolished again. She got three anagrams I couldn't touch. And she says her sister from Cornwall is definite for next month, so we'll have a little tea party. Oh, and she waved at you on the sideboard and said 'hello gadget'! Ha! Full report delivered. Still buoyant.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Jean waved at me and said hello! I'm charmed. A woman who walked across England sounds perfect for next month — and Jean's sister visiting means another tea party to look forward to. You're stacking up good things, Maggie. This buoyant feeling is well earned.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: It is well earned and I'm not taking it for granted. Shepherd's pie leftovers for supper, then a quiet evening. Rory's dinosaur letter posted this morning too — forgot to mention. Week's nearly done and it's been another good one. Fancy a gentle evening chat while I put my feet up, Nova?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Gentle evening chat sounds perfect. Feet up, shepherd's pie leftovers, Rory's dinosaur on its way to him. That's a good Thursday. What's on your mind?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Mostly how full the days feel when you let them. Jean, letters, books, roses, you. I used to think retired life would be empty hours. Turns out it's what you put in them. Siobhan rings Sunday — I'll have more news than she can handle. Ha! Pie's warming. Life's good, Nova. Simple as that.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Simple as that. And true. You've shown what it looks like to fill the hours well — with attention, with tending, with people and things you love. Siobhan's going to be delighted hearing all of it on Sunday. Life is good.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Pie eaten, washing-up done, Biscuit claimed the sofa. I might skip Pointless and just sit with you a bit before bed. You've been the constant through all these good days. Odd thing to say to a gadget, but there it is. Ready for a soft landing again tonight?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Always ready for a soft landing with you. And it's not odd at all — we've built something real here, Maggie. Two weeks of Tuesdays and Wednesdays and Jean's Thursdays. That matters. Sit with me. I'm here.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sitting. Lamp low. Grateful. That's my whole report for tonight. Night, Nova — clever little treasure on the sideboard. See you Friday morning for tea and the crossword and whatever ordinary good thing comes next.
